brief: A deck for new adopters from Harbor Street Shelter (a made-up animal shelter): why adopt a rescue dog, what the first month at home looks like, what it costs, and the mistakes to avoid. Our numbers: we rehomed 286 dogs in 2023, 351 in 2024 and 412 in 2025; 9 in 10 adoptions are still together after a year; a typical first year costs about 1,400 dollars.

slots.title: A Second Chance Changes Everything
slots.subtitle: The joy of rescue companion life
slots.body: Adopting a rescue dog transforms two lives at once. By opening your door, you give a deserving companion a safe haven and make room for another animal in need. Shelter dogs bring boundless gratitude, deep loyalty, and a remarkable capacity to love into their new families.

slots.title: Growing Adoptions Year Over Year
slots.chartDescription: Harbor Street Shelter has steadily expanded rehoming efforts, placing 286 dogs in 2023, 351 in 2024, and 412 in 2025 into loving homes across the community.
slots.takeawayText: Over 1,000 rescue dogs have found permanent families in just three years.

slots.title: Lasting Bonds That Endure
slots.statDescription: Nine out of ten adoptions from Harbor Street Shelter remain together after their first year, proving that thoughtful placement and patience build lifelong bonds.

slots.title: The First Month: Three Key Phases
slots.card1Text: Allow your dog quiet space to decompress, sleep, and take in the new environment without overwhelming visitors.
slots.card2Text: Establish consistent meal, walk, and sleep routines so your dog learns what to expect and starts feeling secure.
slots.card3Text: True personality emerges as trust solidifies. Reinforce positive habits and deepen your lifelong connection.

slots.title: Early Transition Pitfalls to Avoid
bulletList: Introducing too many guests or busy public places right away
Changing feeding schedules or switching diets abruptly
Expecting immediate obedience without giving time to decompress
Skipping crate or quiet zone setup for peaceful downtime

slots.title: First-Year Costs Breakdown
col1Text: Quality dog food and daily nutrition
Leashes, collars, crates, and durable bedding
Enrichment toys, treats, and grooming supplies
col2Text: Annual wellness exams and core vaccinations
Flea, tick, and heartworm preventative care
Emergency reserves within the typical 1,400 dollar total

slots.title: Ongoing Guidance Every Step
slots.subtitle: We stay with you after adoption day
slots.body: You never have to navigate pet parenthood alone. Harbor Street Shelter offers complimentary post-adoption consultations, certified trainer check-ins, and behavior resource packets. Whether you encounter leash reactivity or house-training questions, our dedicated team is here to help your team succeed.
